question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Neither the manager nor the employees **was available.**
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. were available .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is a compound subject joined by **"Neither...nor"**.
 
• When subjects are joined by **"Neither...nor,"** the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• In this case, **"employees"** is plural, so the verb should be **"were available"**.

Correct sentence: *Neither the manager nor the employees **were available**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**

 
 
• When two subjects are joined by **"Neither...nor" or "Either...or,"** the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• For example: **"Neither John nor his friends were available."**
 
• Similarly: **"Either the manager or the employees were present."**
 
 
 
• **Plural Subjects:**
 
 
• When the closest subject is plural, the verb must be plural.
 
• In this case, **"employees"** is plural, so **"were"** is correct.
